When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **6/10**, ALARM vs VIX Spike tier **1/4**, BROAD, backwardation off
Price and breadth signals flag stress, but options markets have not priced a spike yet. Trust the Crash Index for direction, and read the low tier as unspent room, since skew is already active and spike probability sits at **50%**.
⚠ These two disagree: Contrarian score **95**, STRONG BUY vs Regime state **71** with risk off bias, macro regime CONTRACTION at **70%**
The contrarian gauge measures sentiment washout. The regime gauge measures trend and macro pressure. Trust the regime for sizing today and the contrarian score for timing the eventual turn, which needs the VIX tier to stop rising first.
⚠ These two disagree: Composite divergence zone CALM vs Mother jaws score **100**
The composite counts how many of **43** pairs diverge (**44.2%**) and nets bullish against bearish, which keeps the zone calm. The jaws score measures how stretched the worst pairs are. Trust the jaws for fragility in specific relationships.

AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The market is under real stress, and the Crash Index at 6 of 10 says so. The regime state score of 71 shows 4 risk off signals aligned, and the macro regime reads contraction at 70% confidence. Against that, the contrarian score of 95 flags capitulation. You have a washed out market inside a weakening economy.

That split dictates how you position. Cut gross exposure and favor balance sheet quality while the regime holds. Keep a short list of buy candidates for the day sentiment and vol confirm a low. The VIX Spike tier is only 1 of 4, so hedges are still cheap compared with where they will trade if the tier climbs. Buy protection now.

The main risk is a fast move up the vol curve. Skew is active, the spike probability is 50%, and the two active confluences (credit stress and yen safe haven flow) show money already moving defensively. If VIX backwardation turns on and the tier rises above 1, the crash signals win and the contrarian buy waits. If the tier stays at 1 while price stabilizes, the 95 reading earns a staged entry.

Dow Theory generalized · cross-asset divergences
Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means two assets that usually move together or in opposite directions have stopped doing so. Correlation drift is the size of that change, measured as the shift in their relationship between an older window and a recent one.

The composite zone is CALM, with 44.2% of 43 pairs diverging, 13 leaning bullish and 6 bearish for a net bias of minus 7. The jaws score of 100 says the extremes are anything but calm.

The 10 year minus 2 year yield spread went from a correlation of minus 0.61 to plus 0.38, and NVDA against AMD moved from minus 0.91 to plus 0.38. Energy against gold flipped from plus 0.41 to minus 0.25.

Each pair scores 80 (deep divergence). When relationships this old break down at once, hedges built on past correlations stop working, so check what your hedges are actually tied to.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Every region is down over five days, and the damage grows with distance from the US. Europe leads the weakness, with the DAX down 7.3% and the Swiss index down 3.5%.

Asia follows, with Hong Kong down 5.2% and Nikkei down 2.0%. The US holds up best, with the NDX down 1.7% and the Dow down 3.9%.

Crypto trades in a tight band, with SOL down 2.2% and ETH down 3.8%, so it shows no panic. The US is the last to fall, so it carries catch down risk into the session.

The Dow's lag points to pressure on cyclicals and industrials, while tech still holds. A DAX bounce would ease that pressure.

A further slide would put the NDX at risk.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 6/10 · ALARM — 5+ signals aligned, action zone
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

The Crash Index at 6 of 10 and the VIX Spike tier at 1 of 4 disagree, and that gap is coherent. The Crash Index counts stress in price, credit and breadth, so it reacts to damage that has already happened.

The VIX Spike Detector reads how options markets price what comes next. Today the damage is visible while option buyers have not yet paid up for a vol expansion.

Backwardation is off, so the front of the vol curve is not yet above the back. Skew is active and the spike probability is 50%, so protection is starting to cost more at the downside strikes.

Treat the Crash Index as the warning and the VIX tier as the trigger. A rise from tier 1 would close the gap by pushing options toward the price signals.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 6/10 — several signals are aligned, a real stress probability is building.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
